one_liner: Cloud observability platform for monitoring infrastructure, applications, and logs.

evidence.claim: API requests are authenticated with API keys (plus application keys for many endpoints).
evidence.quote: All requests to Datadog's API must be authenticated. Requests that write data require reporting access and require an API key .

evidence.claim: Credentials are created self-serve from Organization Settings once a user has the right permission.
evidence.quote: To add a Datadog application key, navigate to Organization Settings > Application Keys. If you have the permission to create application keys, click New Key.

evidence.claim: OAuth 2.0 is supported for API-based integrations.
evidence.quote: OAuth 2.0 is an industry-standard authorization framework that enables secure access to Datadog APIs without exposing user credentials.

evidence.claim: The public API is a resource-oriented HTTP REST API.
evidence.quote: The Datadog API is an HTTP REST API. The API uses resource-oriented URLs to call the API, uses status codes to indicate the success or failure of requests,

evidence.claim: Datadog's own docs site ships an official MCP server bridging Datadog data to AI agents.
evidence.quote: The Datadog MCP Server acts as a bridge between your observability data in Datadog and any AI agents that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

notes: Datadog is transitioning auth from application keys to scoped, identity-aware PATs/SATs per its blog ('replaces application keys with scoped, identity-aware access using PATs, SATs'), so toolkit auth should anticipate scoped tokens. Official MCP server exists at docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server (vendor-hosted). The supplied material does not state whether a free tier or trial grants API credentials, so access cost is unknown; key creation itself is documented as self-serve within an account. The API reference spans many resource areas (metrics, synthetics, logs, dashboards, monitors, etc.), indicating broad surface area.
